title: Spotify confirms it won’t stop Family Plan sharing verification, but it’s not a ‘crackdown’
snippet: Earlier this week a new method of Spotify Family plan verification came to light and, in its latest earnings call, Spotify says that it’s not a “crackdown,” but also something that doesn’t have an “end date.” more…
fullText:
Earlier this week a new method of Spotify Family plan verification came to light and, in its latest earnings call, Spotify says that it’s not a “crackdown,” but also something that doesn’t have an “end date.”

Like virtually every family sharing subscription, Spotify requires Family Plan members to be in the same physical household, but the music streaming app has been looser in its requirements and enforcement. A new method, though, started popping up recently in the form of a verification QR code that makes it a bit more difficult for remote participants to complete verification, and also threatens to ban users from Family plans for a full year if verification isn’t completed.

Spotify’s ‘QR code verification’ cracks down on sharing and could ban you for a year

Today, Spotify’s Q3 earnings call included a question about Spotify “beginning to crack down on Family Plan subscribers that do not live in the same home.” 

Responding to this, Spotify co-CEO Alex Norström says that this is not a “crackdown,” but a “routine improvement of our verification methods,” and something that Spotify will continue to work on. “This is not something that has an end date,” he said:

	

…this is not as much a crackdown as it is actually a routine improvement of our verification methods for our Family Plan. Family Plan has existed for a long while. It has been around for, I think it is now close to 12, 13 years in Spotify history, and it makes up a pretty significant proportion of our subscriber base. As such, it is important for us to just make sure over time that we improve the verification methods that we have. There are certainly ways, over time, to find holes around it. As that happens, we figure out how to improve it over time. This is not something that has an end date. This is not an implementation that is going to complete. This is just ongoing routine.

Reading between the lines, this is saying that Spotify isn’t going to be backing down from verification methods on its Family Plan sharing. QR codes are only the latest implementation.

Supernatural made a name for itself as the de facto workout app through the COVID era and beyond, and is coming back from the grave as an independent app, starting today.

Workout trends often come and go like the wind, but a few staples hang around long enough to be properly cemented into the “this really works” category. Supernatural is one such example. The VR workout app debuted on April 23, 2020, making it the best way to get a gym-like workout in a world where all the gyms were shut down during the pandemic. Lots of people used it and continued to use it until earlier this year, when Meta closed the studio that made it.

People were devastated. The entire Supernatural community on Facebook was up in arms. But it wasn’t long until Supernatural’s founders announced that they had acquired the rights and would be returning later in 2026 as an independent company, and today is that day.

Meta Quest 3 at Amazon

AMVR FC4M magnetic face pad (you’ll thank me later) at Amazon

Supernatural Early Access is officially launching today, October 21, on Meta’s storefront. You can get a free 7-day trial by downloading the app, and then it’s $20 per month after that. An extended 14-day free trial is available to folks who sign up for the $200/year plan, which grants a $40 annual discount by paying up front.

	

If you haven’t used Supernatural before, you’re about to be very pleasantly surprised. The game features daily coach-led workouts with popular music you’ll love to work out to. Gamers move their bodies around to the beat, smashing flying obstacles with bats, ducking, kicking, and generally getting very sweaty. The whole thing takes place in incredibly realistic environments, which the Supernatural team says are getting a big visual upgrade in the new release.

Today’s early access version launches with thousands of workouts available immediately — with all the coaches you know and love — including hundreds of licensed music tracks, a brand new home environment set in Laguna Torre, a glacial lake in Argentine Patagonia, and the ability to transfer your entire workout history from the old Supernatural app to the new one. I know my colleague, Daniel Bader, will be very happy about that.

Founding members will start with a custom bat, and more rewards are dropping throughout the early access period. Additionally, household accounts can be used to share the experience with up to four people in your home, including individual profiles for each one. Make sure you get a good face pad that’s easy to clean if you do this!

As Supernatural continues to get rebuilt and gets better than ever, users can expect more workouts and music on a weekly cadence, the return of real-time workouts with friends (sign up for the beta now), a new mobile companion app (that pairs with your smartwatch), new destinations, and plenty of rewards for returning and founding members. It’s incredible, and it’s quite frankly mind-blowing to see the entire team return this way, all without the help of Meta.

fullText:
Google Maps in CarPlay now lets you access Gemini when navigating for a conversational driving experience.

	

When using navigation, tapping the Gemini icon on the right edge lets you ask multi-step questions and issue commands like:

“What park is famous for gorgeous views overlooking the city?”

“I want to go at a time when it’s not too busy and the weather will stay nice. Is now a good time?”

This is the first time Google Maps is offering voice assistant functionality in CarPlay. Previously, Google Assistant was only available when using Google Maps navigation directly on your iPhone.

Gemini can also be used to report traffic disruptions with your voice. This matches the navigation experience introduced on Google Maps for Android and iOS last year, while it’s already available in Android Auto.

	

Gemini in Google Maps on Apple CarPlay is available now in the US, while the global rollout is underway.

title: Google gives Pixel 9 another year of free Satellite SOS connectivity
snippet: Google won’t start charging for the Satellite SOS feature on its Pixel 9 series phones just yet, despite the timer having run out. more…
fullText:
Google won’t start charging for the Satellite SOS feature on its Pixel 9 series phones just yet, despite the timer having run out.

Satellite SOS was introduced on the Pixel 9 series and has been in place on every Pixel phone released in the time since. The feature grants your phone access to limited satellite connectivity in emergencies, offering a lifeline in dangerous, off-grid situations. 

But Google only promised this would be free for “the first 2 years after activation.”

A support page footnote still reads:

	

Service included at no additional charge for the first 2 years after activation of devices. Available in select countries and languages. Connection and response times vary based on location, site conditions, and other factors.

Everything you should know about Satellite SOS on Pixel 9 before you ever have to use it

As of August 2026, that timer was up for Pixel 9 series devices. Yet, Google showed no signs of charging for the feature, but it wasn’t exactly clear what would happen next. Now, the company has confirmed that, at least for another year, Satellite SOS on Pixel 9 remains free.

The company confirmed the news to PCMag, saying:

Confirming that we’ve extended this offering, at no additional cost, for one additional year. We have no details to share beyond that at this time.

So far, there have been no hints even behind the scenes of Google introducing a way to charge for Satellite SOS on Pixel phones. Apple, which introduced this functionality prior to Google, recently confirmed that it would also be extending the “free trial” of satellite connections for iPhone 14, 15, and 16, and there’s also no word on what Apple might charge for the feature.

Would you pay for Satellite SOS on your Pixel if Google starts charging for it?

title: Apple Brings M6 Updates to MacBook Pro and iMac Lines
snippet: Designs and pricing stay the same.
fullText:
On the heels of yesterday’s new iPad mini annoucement, Apple has turned its attention to its Mac lineup. Unlike the iPad Mini that received an OLED display and a water-resistant design, today’s Mac updates are mere spec bumps. After debuting its M6 processor with the Mac Mini in August, Apple is bringing the M6 to both its entry-level MacBook Pro and iMac.

M6 means more cores

The M6 chip in the ‌MacBook Pro‌ features a 12-core CPU (two super cores, four performance cores and six efficiency cores) and a 12-core GPU. The previous M5 model had a 10-core CPU (four super cores and six efficiency cores) and a 10-core GPU. 

In addition, the Neural Engine in the M6 doubles the number of cores, with a dual 16-core NE replacing the single 16-core NE from before.

			

More from CNET

Memory bandwidth also increases from 153GB per second to 170GB per second, but this bump comes only when you choose to outfit the MacBook Pro with 24GB or 32GB of memory and not the default 16GB.

Networking improves with support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, and the new laptop can support dual external 4K displays at up to 165Hz, up from 144Hz.

In this era of constantly rising costs, seeing a price remain constant feels like a win. The M6 MacBook Pro starts at the same $1,999 price as the previous model. 

iMac skips from M4 to M6

It’s been nearly two years since the last iMac update, which means Apple’s all-in-one makes the jump from the M4  to the M6 processor. The design (built around a 24-inch, 4.5K Retina display) and color options (blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange and silver) stay the same, as does the $1,499 starting price. 

But now for that $1,499, the M6 iMac has a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU along with the dual 16-core Neural Engine. That’s up from the M4 chip that started with eight CPU cores and eight GPU cores and a single 16-core NE.

The step-up model costs $1,699 and gets you an M6 chip with a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, along with four Thunderbolt 4 ports instead of just a pair. This higher-end model also comes with 2.5Gb Ethernet, which is available as an add-on with the baseline model. The previous M4 iMac offered only Gigabit Ethernet.

Preorders open Wednesday, Oct. 28, for the new M6 MacBook Pro and M6 iMac, with shipping expected to start on Friday, Nov. 6.

Apple’s Pro and Tell week isn’t over. It will culminate with tomorrow’s special event in Los Angeles where Apple is expected to reveal the long-awaited touchscreen MacBook Pro.

snippet: Over the weekend, a handful of iPhone Duo users reported that their inner display had cracked along the hinge. In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple said it is “aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units,” and that affected users can contact AppleCare for a replacement. more…
fullText:
Over the weekend, a handful of iPhone Duo users reported that their inner display had cracked along the hinge. In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple said it is “aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units,” and that affected users can contact AppleCare for a replacement. 

Here is Apple’s full statement: 

“The response to iPhone Duo from early users has been incredibly positive, and we are seeing exciting things from developers who are rapidly updating their apps to take advantage of its unique form factor. We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units. If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement.”

The company says the problem affects a very small number of iPhone Duo units and appears to surface relatively quickly. Most iPhone Duo units are not affected. You do not need AppleCare+ to have your iPhone Duo replaced for this problem. If you bought from a carrier, you should contact AppleCare directly, not your carrier, to get your device replaced. 

Reports of the problem surfaced on Reddit and other forums over the weekend. Affected users report that the inner screens cracked along the center line of the hinge. While a number of user reports on Reddit showing the issue are legitimate, there have been a handful of fake AI-generated reports as well. 

The folks at iFixit have pointed to a few potential causes of the problems, with certain components potentially putting excessive pressure on the display.

title: Are We All Maxxed Out? Dictionary.com Names ‘Maxxing’ Its 2026 Word of the Year
snippet: Data center and unc were on the shortlist of words considered for the tribute.
fullText:
Are you focusmaxxing today? Knowledgemaxxing? Maybe fibermaxxing? Dictionary.com has chosen “maxxing,” which can seemingly be attached as a suffix to any other English word, as its Word of the Year for 2026.

Dictionary.com defines maxxing as “the practice of pursuing an activity to the fullest or optimizing a certain aspect of your life.” It’s not a lot different from older expressions such as taking it to the max, maxing out a credit card or feeling maxed out. Words like max, maximum and maximize have their roots in the Latin maximus — meaning “greatest” or “largest.”

But maxxing takes it to another level. The word has an additional x and can be tacked onto the back of seemingly any word. Dictionary.com said that two of the most common of these in 2026 have been looksmaxxing and tokenmaxxing.

			

More from CNET

Looksmaxxing — maximizing one’s physical appearance — was the most popular internet search term in 2026 for derivations of maxxing, according to Dictionary.com. Certain internet content creators popularized the term and have gained large followings with their sometimes extreme approaches to improving their looks.

Tokenmaxxing is another frequently searched term. In the world of AI, token refers to a small bit of written text that AI language models process to formulate responses. The term tokenmaxxing generally refers to using AI as much as possible at work, as companies integrate AI more and more into workflows. It’s no joke: Some companies are tracking and evaluating their workers on how much and how effectively they use AI in their jobs.

Maxxing can also be used on its own, such as, “Have you been maxxing on anything lately?”

Dictionary.com said the popularity of “maxxing” in all its various uses indicates how much we value optimization, as does the rising use of prefixes super- and ultra- in 2025.

“Whatever we’re doing, we want to push it further,” Dictionary.com reports. “But its expanding uses also reveal how people are responding to that impulse. Some embrace it. Some exaggerate it for laughs. Others flip it on its head to describe stepping away from the relentless pursuit of more. The open question is whether this need for optimization has peaked or if we’ll push even harder next year.”

If you let your imagination fly, you can maxx on anything — dietmaxxing to lose weight, bookmaxxing to read more, bingemaxxing for all that streaming.

Data center among the top 5

Dictionary.com’s shortlist of top words this year included affordability, data center (spelled as two words), odyssey and unc. Affordability has been one of the most common words in politics in the lead-up to the midterms — can people pay for what they need? Data centers are sprouting up all over the US and are either gateways to economic prosperity or harbingers of doom, depending on whom you talk to.

Unc, short for uncle, refers to someone who’s out of touch with Gen Z and Gen Alpha culture; and odyssey cracked the top five thanks to the popularity of The Odyssey, Christopher Nolan’s 2026 film adapted from Homer’s Greek epic about Odysseus’ journey home after the Trojan War.

title: OnePlus starts rolling out stable Android 17 updates early, marking the end of OxygenOS
snippet: OnePlus is now rolling out stable Android 17 updates to OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4, marking the end of OxygenOS as these devices are just the first to transition to ColorOS. more…
fullText:
OnePlus is now rolling out stable Android 17 updates to OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4, marking the end of OxygenOS as these devices are just the first to transition to ColorOS.

OxygenOS has been OnePlus’ skin on top of Android for years. It started off as a “stock” skin with some added features, but eventually transitioned into a global-optimized version of Oppo’s ColorOS. So it wasn’t a surprise that, when OnePlus shut down most of its global operations, it was also announced that OxygenOS would go away with existing devices updating to ColorOS. 

Starting in India, ColorOS 17 based on Android 17 is rolling out to the OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4. The update has been in beta for a while now, but today marks the start of the stable rollout.

OnePlus summarizes ColorOS 17, saying:

	

ColorOS 17 is here, bringing a new wave of smarter experiences, smoother interactions, and more ways to make your phone work around you… At the heart of ColorOS 17 is an idea we believe in: Flow with AI, Flow Everywhere. Technology should feel less like something you have to figure out and more like something that naturally keeps up with you. From making everyday interactions feel more fluid to turning ideas into finished work with AI, we’re bringing intelligence closer to the moments that matter, helping you move between tasks, devices, and experiences with less friction.

Originally, OnePlus’ timeline put the first updates on October 29.

Other devices confirmed to be updated include last-gen flagships and an assortment of Nord devices, but OnePlus 15 and Pad 4 are the only two for this first wave. Presumably, the update will expand to other regions in the coming days. The next wave lands on October 30 and includes OnePlus 13.

title: iOS 27.2: Three new features coming to your iPhone next week
snippet: iOS 27.2 is about to launch, arriving as the next big iPhone update—iOS 27.1 is iPhone Duo-only. Here are three new features coming next week with iOS 27.2. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.2 is about to launch, arriving as the next big iPhone update—iOS 27.1 is iPhone Duo-only. Here are three new features coming next week with iOS 27.2.

#1: Dual Capture for Group FaceTime

FaceTime got one of its biggest upgrades in years with iOS 27. 

On compatible iPhone models, Dual Capture lets you display both your front and rear camera views at the same time. Just tap the ‘Flip’ button and the back camera will go live while the front camera remains active.

And in iOS 27.2, the feature gets even better by adding support for Group FaceTime calls.

iOS 27 only lets you use Dual Capture in one-on-one calls, but with iOS 27.2 it’s available for Group FaceTime too.

#2: Apple Podcasts overhauls ‘Up Next’ queue

Apple Podcasts gets a key change in iOS 27.2 that I’m a big fan of.

The previous ‘Up Next’ queue at the top of the app’s Home tab is now split into two new sections:

New Episodes replaces Up Next, and contains the latest releases for shows you follow

Continue Playing is brand new, located directly below New Episodes as a hub for all in-progress shows

I’ve criticized the Up Next feature before for being cluttered and confusing, so I’m very excited to see this change. After testing it during the beta, I think it’s a huge improvement that helps users better keep track of everything they’re listening to.

#3: Apple TV app supports user profiles

Apple’s TV app is about to support user profiles on iPhone, bringing the feature over from tvOS to iOS for the first time.

When you first launch the TV app in iOS 27.2, you’ll see a new profile selection screen. You can easily disable it from ever showing up again. But if your child ever watches videos on your iPhone, you might be very glad about this new feature.

With profiles, the Apple TV app can change which content it displays and recommends based on the selected viewer. And importantly, when a child’s profile is active, they’ll only see age-appropriate series and movies from Apple. So not only does your own personal viewing queue stay uncluttered, but you also ensure your child doesn’t see something they shouldn’t.

title: Samsung confirms a list of Galaxy phones and tablets getting Android 17 updates
snippet: Samsung has confirmed a list of Galaxy devices that are set to get its Android 17-based One UI 9 update in at least one region, which tells us what to expect globally in the coming months. more…
fullText:
Samsung has confirmed a list of Galaxy devices that are set to get its Android 17-based One UI 9 update in at least one region, which tells us what to expect globally in the coming months.

One UI 9 started rolling out with the Galaxy S26 series in September and, in the time since, has expanded to a bunch of last-gen Galaxy smartphones. What’s next? Samsung has confirmed an official list of Galaxy smartphones and tablets that will be getting Android 17-based One UI 9 updates.

title: Google Messages rolling out Enhanced Protection mode against spam and scams
snippet: Following the announcement earlier this month, Google Messages for Android is rolling out an Enhanced Protection mode to counter spam and scams. more…
fullText:
Following the announcement earlier this month, Google Messages for Android is rolling out an Enhanced Protection mode to counter spam and scams.

To date, Google Messages has offered Standard Protection to block “spam and suspected harmful links.” Enhanced Protection introduces “Advanced detection to prevent spam and scams.” There are three core features at launch.

Scam Detection will leverage “cloud Gemini models to evaluate complex message context and understand a scammer’s intent more quickly when you’re in a conversation with an unknown sender.” Compared to the existing on-device detection, this approach is better at identifying “novel and sophisticated attacks.”

It uses Android’s Private AI Compute feature to encrypt messages and process them in a secure space that is “private to you and not available to anyone else, including Google.”

	

Meanwhile, enhanced link protections use the on-device Gemini Nano model and real-time web signals to evaluate whether an unfamiliar link is trustworthy before you tap. This feature is available on the Pixel 10+, Samsung Galaxy S26 series, Z Flip 8, Z Fold 8, and “other select devices.”

	

The final update redesigns warnings to give you additional time and more context to “pause before tapping links” sent by numbers not in your contacts.

Enhanced Protection is an opt-in feature. To enable, go to Google Messages settings > Protection & safety. Instead of an on/off toggle, you’ll find three options:

Enhanced protection

Standard protection

No protection (not recommended)

We’re seeing this available with the latest Google Messages beta (version 20261020_00_RC00).

title: Billionaire Palmer Luckey isn’t leaving California over the wealth tax
snippet: "It's causing a lot of people to run who I don't want to be running," native Californian Palmer Luckey said. "But I'm planning on staying in California. I'm going to keep fighting it."
fullText:
Palmer Luckey has been a California billionaire since he was 21 years old, when he sold his first company, virtual reality headset maker Oculus VR, to Facebook for $2 billion in 2014. His current company, defense tech firm Anduril, is headquartered in in Costa Mesa, California, not far from Long Beach, where Luckey grew up. And Anduril is worth far more. It was last valued at $61 billion.

While Luckey clearly despises the proposed California billionaire wealth tax, a ballot measure that would tax the net worth of the state’s richest residents, he said he’s not leaving California over it.

“I think that this tax act, if you can call it a tax, is going to cause a lot of problems. It’s causing a lot of people to run who I don’t want to be running. It’s going to cause companies that I work with to leave the state, which is a problem for me. As of right now, though, I’m not running. I am staying. I think California is something special. I want to fight for California,” Luckey said during an invite-only press conference on Monday.

He added that he’s felt pressure from other billionaires to declare his intention to leave.

“This has been a point of friction between me and some of my other billionaire friends,” he said. “They’ve said things like ‘Palmer, you have to have solidarity for us. You can’t enable these really bad policies. If you stay and if you don’t leave, it’s going to show them that there’s no consequences.’ I empathize with that argument, but it’s not one that I’m going to participate in right now because I still believe that we can fix things.”

Luckey added that it’s not the idea of paying taxes that he takes issue with, but that the bill is sponsored by specific union, a unit of the United Healthcare Workers, that wants to use the money the tax would raise “for their uses,” he said. The measure’s sponsors say the money will be used for “health care, education, and food assistance” programs in the state, and they specifically name Medi-Cal, California’s health coverage program for low-income residents.

Another issue is for Luckey, as for others, is how the proposal would assess the tax owed, as well as the penalties. It would tax “wealth” including unrealized assets that haven’t been sold, and illiquid assets that are hard to turn into cash. And penalties can be assessed as high as 40%.

“It’s almost like a seizure of future wealth in that way. That’s not even the real problem. The biggest problem is the tax on control of your own company,” he said. According to the Tax Foundation, a tax policy think tank, the proposal treat someone someone with voting control as owning at least that same share of the company. This would affect founders with super-voting shares, which carry extra votes per share, because they may own only a minority of the company. A founder with 40% of the votes but 10% of the ownership, for example, could be taxed as if they owned at least 40%, and selling all their shares might not cover the bill. (The measure’s drafters say that reading is mistaken, arguing that super-voting shares are publicly traded assets and are valued differently.)

“I’m a founder who’s raised a bunch of money, I’ve diluted myself a lot. I’ve given equity to my employees,” Luckey said of his own situation. “My employees have more equity in Anduril than me. I’ve given a lot of equity out to people, but what I have done is I’ve preserved the voting rights so that as those employees sell their shares to pay off their home loans or whatever, that the voting control doesn’t go to other people outside the company.”

He also said that if he were ever to leave, “I lose all those voting rights. My voting rights only stick as long as I’m an American citizen living in America, running Anduril.” The condition makes sense given that Anduril is primarily a defense contractor selling equipment to the U.S. military.

In Luckey’s case, he believes he could owe 5% of Anduril’s $61 billion, a bill of around $3 billion, just on that asset alone. (For comparison, Larry Page, the Google co-founder who did leave California, still has 27% voting control of Alphabet, Google’s parent company, which has a market value of just under $4 trillion.)

“But I’m planning on staying in California. I’m going to keep fighting it,” he said. “I’m hoping that this doesn’t pass. I’m hoping if it does pass, that there are legal challenges to say, “Hey, you can’t post facto seize people’s past and future wealth, nor can you tax their voting interests in their own company. That’s truly unprecedented. That is not a tax on ownership. It is a tax on control.”

title: Iron Man himself now officially endorses Snap’s latest smart glasses
snippet: Snap Specs are available for pre-order now, and actor Robert Downey Jr. is joining the team after he said he “was absolutely sold on Specs within 40 seconds.” more…
fullText:
Snap Specs are available for pre-order now, and actor Robert Downey Jr. is joining the team after he said he “was absolutely sold on Specs within 40 seconds.”

That makes Robert Downey Jr. the latest big-name partnership from Snap, as the company gets ready to launch its first true consumer-ready smart glasses, simply called Specs. Downey Jr. join the team at Snap as the honorary Chief Customer Experience Officer (CCEO), putting him in charge of showing the world just how close to his Iron Man roots these glasses really are.

Downey Jr. launched a new series of videos on the Snap YouTube channel, helping showcase all the cool things Specs can do. From helping you paint better with an AR overlay to watching movies in bed, and even letting Specs calculate where you need to hit the ball on a putting green, Downey Jr. is pulling out all the stops to get you interested in these $2,200 smart glasses.

Snap is clearly challenging Meta’s market leadership in the XR category with a product that combines elements of Meta Ray-Ban Display Glasses and the upcoming Meta VR Glasses. Specs are a completely standalone pair of smart glasses with displays in each lens, plus full hand-tracking support that’s typically only found on a bulkier VR headset.

	

Snap has been building up to the Specs release since 2016 (not a typo). The company has released several experimental developer-only smart glasses during that time, all of which were significantly bulkier than Specs now looks, with huge improvements between each generation.

In addition to the clear Iron Man nod, Snap has also partnered with HBO to launch a Specs Harry Potter experience to coincide with the new HBO show, plus an official partnership with the NBA. The first original episode of Downey Jr.’s SPECS-focused videos will debut during Game 1 of the World Series on Friday, October 23. You can preorder Specs from Snap right now.

title: New iPad mini vs previous model: Here’s everything new
snippet: Apple unveiled a new iPad mini today, and it’s a big upgrade over the previous model. Here’s everything new. more…
fullText:
Apple unveiled a new iPad mini today, and it’s a big upgrade over the previous model. Here’s everything new.

Design: Thinner, reduced bezels, camera repositioned, and new colors

The new iPad mini look similar to the previous model, but also fresh and more modern thanks to two main design changes:

It’s thinner than ever, with a depth of 5.4mm compared to 6.3mm on the last model

Bezels are now 24% smaller than before

You may or may not notice, but the new mini is also slightly more narrow, measuring 132.6mm wide vs 134.8mm. And it weighs less: 255 grams vs 293 for Wi-Fi models.

The front-facing Center Stage camera is now positioned on the landscape side of the device rather than portrait.

Apple now offers the iPad mini in two colors: Midnight and Starlight. Previously more options were available, including Space Gray and Starlight, but the latest colors still have an updated look.

Display: Larger display with OLED, optional nano-texture

Thanks to the reduced bezels, the new iPad mini now has a larger, 8.5-inch display. The previous model’s was only 8.3 inches.

Perhaps a more significant change is that the display is OLED, a big upgrade from the LCD technology used before. Apple says this enables “pixel-level lighting control for much deeper blacks and support for the P3 wide color gamut for more vivid and accurate imagery.”

The display gets much brighter than before too, with peak brightness of 1200 nits, double the previous max of 600. Standard SDR and HDR brightness is 600 nits, up from 500. It also supports 1-nit minimum brightness for use in dim environments.

Apple now lets you optionally choose a nano-texture display on 256GB models and up. iPad mini has never previously offered nano-texture.

Performance: A20 Pro vs A17 Pro

The new iPad mini has an A20 Pro chip, Apple’s most powerful mobile processor that first debuted in iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. The previous generation had an A17 Pro. Per Apple:

A20 Pro delivers a giant leap in performance for iPad mini, significantly boosting graphics and AI-intensive tasks. It is built using Apple’s latest 2-nanometer process technology and a new package inspired by M-series chips. Powered by a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core, iPad mini delivers up to 4.5x faster AI performance than the previous generation — perfect for AI tasks ranging from running on-device models in creative apps to running local LLMs. And with the latest graphics architecture, including dynamic caching and hardware-accelerated mesh shading and ray tracing, graphics performance jumps by up to 2.7x — great for gaming and 3D rendering. A20 Pro also features up to a 6-core CPU for up to 60 percent faster multithreaded performance for everyday tasks like editing photos and working across apps.

A20 Pro also brings 2x increase in unified memory bandwidth.

One key detail worth noting is that the new iPad mini uses a binned A20 Pro chip in all but the high-end 512GB model. Not only does the binned chip have only 5 CPU cores rather than 6, it also lacks the Dual 16-core Neural Engine. Instead, you get the standard 16-core Neural Engine.

So if you’re comparing performance, Apple’s “up to” quotes refer to the 512GB model.

Acoustic Display speakers and IP67 water and dust resistance

Instead of the previous traditional stereo speaker setup, the new iPad mini uses “an innovative Acoustic Display” for audio, which Apple says delivers:

an even better audio experience when gaming, watching videos, or editing content. Specially designed woofers are paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume. In addition, custom tweeters are now hidden between the glass and aluminum enclosure for clearer highs.

The Acoustic Display has a sealed enclosure which enables iPad mini to offer IP67 water and dust resistance. This makes it more versatile than before.

Wireless connectivity, fast charging, and more

Apple’s N1 and C2 chips comes to the iPad mini, enabling the following connectivity improvements:

New iPad mini

Previous iPad mini

Wi-Fi

Wi-Fi 7

Wi-Fi 6E

Bluetooth

Bluetooth 6

Bluetooth 5.3

Cellular

Apple C2

Qualcomm

Additionally, though Apple didn’t give specific fast charging details for its last iPad mini, the new model supports: “Up to 50% charge in 30 minutes with a 35W adapter or higher.”

Finally, Apple also notes that the new iPad mini “supports extended display mode when connected to an external display, great for users multitasking with windowed apps.” Previously only mirroring was available, whereas this sounds like a full-fledged extended display feature.

Pricing and availability

fullText:
After the stacked card list redesign, Google Wallet for Android is gaining a notifications feed and support for more passports.

On the homepage, you’ll see a notification bell icon next to the profile switcher in the top-right corner. Tapping opens a feed with “updates about items in Wallet.”

Update 10/23: Following Brazil, Singapore, Taiwan, United Kingdom, and the United States of America, we’re starting to see the ability to add Estonia, Ireland, Italy, and Spain.

To add a passport, tap the ‘plus’ FAB at the bottom of Google Wallet > IDs & personal info > ID pass. The registration process involves scanning your passport info page and security chip. Afterward, you have to record a video of your face. You’ll get a notification once verification is complete.

title: Android has always been chaotic in the best ways possible
snippet: Good morning. Today I’m mourning the end of BioWare, running my Google TV setup through Claude to remove all the bloatware, watching all the iPhone Duo reviews without spending $2,000, and attempting to understand everything I can about PHP in light of two massive vulnerabilities that AI helped uncover. fullText:
Good morning. Today I’m mourning the end of BioWare, running my Google TV setup through Claude to remove all the bloatware, watching all the iPhone Duo reviews without spending $2,000, and attempting to understand everything I can about PHP in light of two massive vulnerabilities that AI helped uncover.

As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

⭐️ Starred

The through-line in every iPhone Duo review yesterday was this: excellent hardware (though a bit too heavy) and a chaotic software experience. When Apple’s foldable launches on Friday, it will remind early adopters of what Android used to feel like whenever a new form factor was introduced: exciting, janky, and slightly aggravating.

	

I think 9to5Google readers understand that Android is for tweakers. It’s why so many of you sign up for Android betas on daily-driver hardware; it’s why there’s a thriving community of indie developers filling gaps in the ecosystem. Android’s freedom and flexibility (and cost) make it particularly well suited to the cavalcade of use cases and designs we see in the market today.

That openness confers other, more nebulous benefits; it’s far easier to emulate games on Android along with other legally grey activities that won’t be mentioned here. If there’s something you want to do on Android, chances are you can figure out a way to do it.

It seems like the iPhone Duo’s early adopters will be faced with a similar conundrum: the ability to do more on a device that is likely to frustrate and delight in equal measure. As Ben explains in his iPhone Duo review roundup, “the app situation clearly seems to be running into the same early problems as Android foldables hit. Apps simply aren’t optimized for a radically new form factor yet.”

But as with all things iPhone, app and software improvements are likely to come quickly and consistently over the next few months and years. Ben eloquently sums up the situation: “Apple has a vision for its foldable and, while it’s tripped up on a few things on attempt #1, it’s undeniably a good start.”

✉️ Inbox

Galaxy S27 might drop to 8GB of RAM; other Android phones could go back to 4GB. Not sure I entirely believe this rumor, but it is true that Google has been making Android more memory-efficient, so maybe it is true?

ModRetro’s Chromatic is more transparent and cheaper than ever; how could I not love it? This product feels like the physical manifestation of using X.

Spotify podcast memberships let you support your favorite shows and get added perks. I support this feature, but the continued fragmentation of the podcast subscription ecosystem is driving me crazy.

Iron Man himself now officially endorses Snap’s latest smart glasses. Because he’s the only person who can afford to buy them.

Older Pixel phones appear to be getting Google’s new 3D emoji. Depending on who you ask, this is a good thing or a terrible thing.

Google says Chrome’s Safe Browsing Enhanced Protection mode makes users 10x safer. Perfect timing with yesterday’s PHP vulnerabilities.

You can cut your cell phone bill to $10/month or get a Pixel 11 for $400 right now – here’s how. Some decent deals from Mint Mobile (#notsponsored).

YouTube starts hiding the dislike button on normal videos. This makes sense to me; dislike buttons used to be there to help shape your algorithm, but there are so many other ways to do that today that its existence feels unnecessary.

Google upgrading Gemini for Android Auto with Personal Intelligence. I can’t wait to ask Gemini about that mole on my back while driving my in-laws around the city.

Google Maps on CarPlay rolling out Gemini when navigating

Android 17 QPR3 Beta 2 for Pixel rolling out with 21 fixes. (Almost) nothing to see here.

Here’s everything new in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 2 [Gallery]

Samsung has updated these Galaxy devices to Android 17

Google Pixel’s solution to using Face Unlock in the dark seems to be just blinding you

The wide folds are coming; foldable display shipments to increase by 44% in 2026, analysts say. This has been a very good year for book-style foldables, and the momentum is slated to continue into 2027.

OpenAI GPT models are coming to Google Antigravity ‘soon,’ Cloud ‘in the coming weeks’. OpenAI and Microsoft continue their very public divorce.

➡️ FWD:

This section has some of our favorite stuff from around the internet. Great videos, weird memes, fun reads, recommended apps, whatever. Send us your recommendations!

I was the guest on this week’s Sideload episode, and we talked about my favorite thing: AI. In particular, how we use AI in our daily lives.

One thing we touched on that I’m going to delve into in a future newsletter is whether Google is actually behind the competition with Gemini. With the recent release of Gemini 4 Argon, it’s clear the company is close to the frontier, but the more important question to answer is whether Gemini is a good product. I make the argument that it is, especially because Google has its tendrils in every part of my life, from email to search to maps, and that makes Gemini’s answers far more useful when I ask it questions of a personal nature. That it has a 25% market share right now is almost accidental; so many people are forced to interact with Gemini in one way or another through Google’s various products.

It’s also bizarre that Google hasn’t figured out a way to compete with Meta on the personal agent front. On its earnings call, Meta said that Muse has been used by over 10 million people, and 25% of them use it every day. Google has Spark, but it’s not in the same league in terms of functionality or mindshare.

Google is unquestionably behind Anthropic and OpenAI where the money is made: in the enterprise. Antigravity is a subpar harness, and Argon is a capable but unspectacular coding agent.

Nevertheless, Google has the money, the user base, and, most importantly, the incentive to keep going after the top labs. In an interview this week with Alex Kantrowitz, CEO Sundar Pichai said that he is committed to the frontier at all costs, and that Google Cloud compute capacity is being reallocated in 2027 to train state-of-the-art models.

Claude Duet is Anthropic’s proactive AI agent answer to Muse and OpenAI’s Dots

It’s almost Thanksgiving travel season, which means it’s time to re-up one of the best Onion videos about the places our souls go to die: airports.

As mentioned above, Supernatural is relaunching on the Quest as a new independent app with the original owners and much of the same crew. When Meta announced that it was laying off much of its Reality Labs division and shutting Supernatural down, it didn’t look good for the future of what I consider the best VR workout app ever made. But by the summer, it was announced that Meta had negotiated a sale of the brand and IP (but not the code), which allowed the formation of Supernatural Health.

Launching this week in Early Access, it’s now double what it used to cost — $200 a year — but it’s one of the few subscriptions I look forward to paying. If you’re a Quest owner, I cannot recommend it highly enough.

title: Will Apple’s overhauled MacBook Pro finally offer 5G cellular support?
snippet: This week, Apple will be overhauling the MacBook Pro for the first time since 2021. OLED, touch support, and a significantly lighter design are expected. Another rumor for the new MacBook Pros has been cellular support, though it’s been unclear if that’s actually going to ship. more…
fullText:
This week, Apple will be overhauling the MacBook Pro for the first time since 2021. OLED, touch support, and a significantly lighter design are expected. Another rumor for the new MacBook Pros has been cellular support, though it’s been unclear if that’s actually going to ship.

To recap, Apple is expected to unveil its first touchscreen MacBooks at its ‘Pro and tell’ experience on October 28 in LA. It likely won’t be a streamed event, just a hands-on experience for influencers and media. At that event, we should be seeing the OLED iPad mini, OLED MacBook Pro, as well as a refreshed iMac and 14″ base model MacBook Pro, both with the M6 chip.

Cellular MacBook on the way?

If Apple were to ship a cellular MacBook, it would likely utilize the C2 modem seen in iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. Even though we don’t know for sure if this weeks new MacBooks will offer cellular, we have a number of hints to suggest so.

In 2024, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman initially reported that Apple was investigating cellular MacBooks for as early as 2026. Back then, he reported that Apple was testing its second generation modem with these MacBooks, which we can assume is the C2.

Additionally, last year, Filipe Esposito reported at Macworld that Apple was testing configurations of an M5 Pro-based MacBook Pro with Apple’s C1 modem. Of course, this is just testing, but the fact that it was with an M5 Pro chip is interesting given the fact that these new MacBooks this week will debut with the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, rather than M6-based chips.

Since then, we haven’t had any substantive leaks regarding cellular support in the MacBook Pro lineup. That said, we haven’t had any leaks explicitly ruling it out, either. One way or the other, it should only be a matter of days until we know for sure.

Strava improves route planning and discovery

Last week, exercise-tracking platform Strava announced a new expansion of its strength training features, adding coach-designed guided workouts with live set and rep tracking.

Today, the company announced yet another set of features, this time focused on making it easier for users to find, plan, and navigate routes for outdoor activities.

More Intuitive Search  – Finding your favorite route has never been easier. Head to the Maps tab and search for route names or points of interest for your next run, walk, hike or ride. Search for places in your own words with results matched to intent.

Improved Route Inventory – Expanded and better-curated routes so users have a broader set of  options to choose from before they ever leave the house.

Redesigned Route Cards – Better assess which route to take by evaluating routes using photos and activity data from Strava users.

Offline Maps – Stay active, even when you don’t have signal. When offline, your saved routes appear right on your home screen so you can reach your destination with confidence. Users can also start and save a workout in Offline Mode, and the finished adventure will upload as soon as service is restored again.

Strava added that subscribers will soon get access to turn-by-turn audio directions, allowing them to “explore somewhere new with confidence” during their walks, hikes, or runs.

Additionally, Strava will expand route details with community-generated tags and descriptions highlighting points of interest along the way, while bringing route discovery to the web, allowing users to browse routes and explore maps from their browsers.

title: MacBook Neo helps Apple soften the blow of global PC market downturn, per report
snippet: A new Counterpoint Research report on global PC shipments for Q3 2026 shows Apple outperforming the broader market, with the MacBook Neo helping cushion the impact of declining demand. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A new Counterpoint Research report on global PC shipments for Q3 2026 shows Apple outperforming the broader market, with the MacBook Neo helping cushion the impact of declining demand. Here are the details.

In a new report released today, Counterpoint Research says global PC shipments plunged 21% during Q3 2026, compared with the year-ago period.

In absolute numbers, Counterpoint says global shipments totaled 57 million units, with Lenovo leading the market with a 26.3% share, despite a 23% year-over-year decline.

HP held second place with an 18.1% share and a 31% decline in shipments, followed by Dell (13.3% share, down 25%), Apple (9.8% share, down 11%), and ASUS, which rounded out the top five with a 9.2% share and a 7% decline. Other vendors accounted for the remaining 23.3% of the market, with shipments down 16% year over year.

Here’s Counterpoint on Apple’s performance for the quarter:

“Apple’s shipments declined 11% YoY to 5.6 million units, giving it a 9.8% market share, up from 8.7% a year earlier. The MacBook Neo helped cushion the decline, allowing Apple to outperform the overall market.”

Commenting on the results, Counterpoint Research senior analyst Minsoo Kang noted that Apple and ASUS outperformed the broader market “through differentiated product portfolios and competitive positioning.”

As most 9to5Mac readers are probably guessing by now, rising memory and other component costs were major contributors to the market-wide downturn. Counterpoint says higher PC prices discouraged consumers from upgrading their devices and weakened demand across the industry.

According to Counterpoint’s data, contract prices for 8GB DDR4 RAM modules rose 24% quarter over quarter in Q3 2026, while 1TB NVMe SSD prices increased 29%.

Looking ahead, Counterpoint expects RAM prices to rise another 13% in Q4 and 15% in Q1 2027, while SSD prices are projected to increase 11% in Q4 before stabilizing in early 2027.

title: Fusion startups are giving the government shares in exchange for awards. Is it worth it?
snippet: Fusion startups face a new challenge, one unrelated to plasma physics: Give the government shares in exchange for funding awards or go it alone?
fullText:
The U.S. government has long had an on-again, off-again relationship with the fusion power sector. As of last week, it’s definitely back on.

Helion and Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS) received awards totaling $260 million from the Department of Commerce under the CHIPS and Science Act, the 2022 law that funds domestic semiconductor development, to develop advanced semiconductors used to help power and control their reactors. Helion landed $175 million, while CFS reeled in $85 million.

But as with many recent government awards, these come with strings attached. Helion and CFS have agreed to give the government nonvoting shares in return. With these awards, the fusion industry is finally getting the government’s attention, though maybe not the sort it envisioned. 

In the past, government support for a startup meant nondilutive capital, meaning money that doesn’t shrink existing investors’ ownership percentages, while giving the company a bigger war chest. Investors loved the deals because it meant their startups got more money without them having to pony up. The government doled out the cash to boost American innovation, though it also meant that, in most cases, the government didn’t directly benefit when it picked a winner. 

The Trump administration has been pushing to change that calculus.

Small awards with big consequences?

For both companies, the total dollar amount pales in comparison to how much each has raised. CFS has raised about $4 billion, while Helion is close behind with $3.2 billion in committed capital. The awards are perhaps more important as signals that, after years of cutting and then trickling out fusion funding, the U.S. government is back in the game.

Fusion, which generates power by fusing atoms together as the sun does, is an expensive endeavor, requiring exotic materials, sophisticated computer modeling, and complex manufacturing. Progress over the last decade has attracted private investors who have bet more than $14 billion that one or more companies will be able to put a power plant on the grid.

Yet according to the Fusion Industry Association, the sector’s trade group, that’s still not enough to beat other countries in the race. Last year, the trade group called on the federal government to inject a one-time infusion of $10 billion into the sector, with $5.4 billion intended for fusion startups.

“Other nations are moving aggressively to accelerate their commercial fusion industries, pouring billions in state-backed efforts to win the race to fusion power,” a spokesperson for CFS told TechCrunch. CFS is a member of the Fusion Industry Association. “The $10 billion ask is designed to build out the research infrastructure in the DOE’s Fusion Roadmap and be catalytic for the U.S. domestic fusion industry to compete with China.”

Until recently, the federal government had been dribbling out dollars for fusion. The Biden administration introduced the Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program, a Department of Energy program that pays companies as they hit technical goals, but the dollar amounts were paltry; less than $50 million was distributed in the first couple years. More recent awards were a little bigger, but still well shy of money the Fusion Industry Association has called for.

Now, with two companies getting $260 million, it looks like the lobbying may be starting to pay off, though not quite as planned as it comes from Commerce rather than the research budget the Fusion Industry Association sought, and it carries equity strings.

The Fusion Industry Association’s lobbying campaign did not include conversations about equity stakes in exchange for awards, a person familiar with the matter told TechCrunch. Yet Helion said the government will receive $175 million in nonvoting equity based on its Series G round, which valued the company at $15.5 billion. That works out to a stake of roughly 1%. The government’s stake in CFS will also be nonvoting and based on the company’s most recent valuation, which CFS has not shared publicly. That means the size of the government’s stake in CFS is not known.

“This type of structure has become more common in large U.S. government investments in recent years,” David Kirtley, co-founder and CEO of Helion, told TechCrunch in a statement. “This approach aligns the interests of Helion and the U.S. taxpayer around our commercial success.”

The CFS spokesperson echoed those comments. “This U.S. equity stake will enable the U.S. taxpayer to participate in the upside of our commercial success in exchange for investing in important research and development that supports the growth of an American commercial fusion industry.”

Not alone

Helion and CFS are the latest in a series of companies that have seen the government take a stake in exchange for federal dollars. 

Last year, critical minerals supplier MP Materials gave the government a 15% stake in exchange for a $400 million investment coupled with a $150 million loan, offtake agreements (which are guaranteed purchases of its output), and profit sharing. Another critical minerals company, USA Rare Earth, gave up a 10% stake for a $277 million award and a $1.3 billion loan. And Intel set an even more awkward precedent. The Biden administration had already awarded the company $8.9 billion that hadn’t yet been paid out. Last year, the Trump administration turned that money into a roughly 10% stake in Intel. The list goes on.

Outside the U.S., Germany-based fusion startup Proxima Fusion confirmed to TechCrunch that the German government and the European Union are on its cap table. It also has received equity investments from German government-backed funds, including SPRIND (Germany’s federal agency for disruptive innovation) and DCTF (Deutsche Climate Tech Fonds).

Not every fusion startup that has worked with the government has given up equity. Thea Energy and Avalanche Energy, which have received federal awards and contracts, and Pacific Fusion, which has partnered with federal labs, confirmed to TechCrunch that they have not given the government a stake. Inertia Enterprises also told TechCrunch that it had not given the government any equity; the startup has a public-private partnership with the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory to commercialize the fusion technology developed there.

So far, it’s just a handful of startups that have agreed to government stakes in exchange for awards. Still, it could set the tone for the industry.

By directly investing in fusion startups, the Trump administration is signaling that fusion power is a strategic priority for the U.S. Such backing could boost investor confidence, though it could just as easily have a chilling effect on private investment. VCs will now have to weigh whether the dilution from a government stake is worth the trade-off. And what happens to cap tables in case of pay-to-play rounds or wind-downs? Who gets priority?

The fusion industry may have raised billions of dollars in recent years, but it will need billions more to deliver on its promises. Federal awards used to be no-brainers when it came time to scale up. Now they’ve grown more complicated. Will the new bargains be worth it?

title: Rivian Halloween Update Turns R1, R2 Into Ghostbusting EVs Through Nov. 2
snippet: The over-the-air update adds themed lights, sounds, a scavenger hunt and a parked-only arcade game.
fullText:
Halloween is one of my family’s favorite holidays, a sentiment clearly shared by somebody at Rivian. Every October, owners of its electric trucks and SUVs can activate Halloween Mode, which changes the exterior lights, sounds and graphics on the infotainment display to match the spookiest season. It’s pretty fun.

This year, Halloween Mode on the R1S, R1T and R2 EVs has become a Ghostbusters–themed experience that Rivian says changes each of its EVs “into a ghost-hunting machine.” The over-the-air update adds lights and sounds, easter eggs and hidden clues in the digital infotainment system, a tie-in with the Rivian Assistant voice control system, and an arcade-style Halloween game that can be played while parked.

The update, developed in collaboration with Sony Pictures, is available now and runs through Nov. 2.

			

More from CNET

The seasonal mode features custom lights and sounds while parked.Rivian

Who ya gonna call?

A new in-vehicle Ghostbusters app bundles the seasonal features into a single red toggle, accessible while parked. Tapping it syncs the EV’s interior and exterior lighting and themed audio to match the Ghostbusters’ car, the Specialized Electronical Vehicular Device (or Ecto-1). Second-generation R1 and R2 owners can also choose from Proton Pack, Slimer, Ghost Trap, or Peter Venkman themes. R1 Gen 1 owners only get the main Ecto-1 theme, but each option pairs a unique exterior LED sequence with a matching audio track. The EV can also be set to automatically trigger a random themed light-and-sound show whenever someone walks past, giving trick-or-treaters a fun surprise.

Inside, the dashboard and rear displays transform to match Ecto-1’s control panels, playing a version of the iconic Ray Parker Jr. Ghostbusters theme song. The Rivian mobile and smartwatch apps also update to match the vehicle’s controls, allowing owners to trigger Ecto-1’s siren and flashing lights from outside the vehicle.

Inside, the various displays are transformed to match the controls and instruments of the Ecto-1 car from the films.Rivian

In addition to putting on a show for passersby, the spooky infotainment mode features clues hidden throughout the EV’s menus that can be tapped to reveal secret characters — like Slimer and Rivian’s Ghost Guard — triggering animations, audio and easter eggs. Even the Rivian Assistant voice command system gets in on the act, taking on an eerie tone for the season, triggering light shows with spoken commands, reading clues for the in-dash scavenger hunt and playing sound effects on request.

Rounding out the update is Mallow Mash, an arcade game accessible from the main touchscreen where players race against the clock to pop mini Stay Puft Marshmallow Men. The full creature feature set — including the scavenger hunt, the arcade game and most of the lights and sounds — is only available when the vehicle is in park. However, the touchscreen’s visual theme will remain active if switched before driving, so you can take the show on the road. 

The update also themes the Rivian mobile and smartwatch apps to match the Ghostbustin’ theme.Rivian

To get in on the fun, both the vehicle software and the Rivian mobile app need to be up to date. Once updated, look for a prompt on the driver display that asks whether you’d like to “hunt some ghosts” and opens the Ghostbusters app.

The real Ecto-R1

In addition to the seasonal software, Rivian also built a few physical homages to the original Ecto-1 based on its R1S. Dubbed the Ecto-R1, the full-size electric SUV features white paint on the body and 22-inch Aero wheels, red graphics running the length of the chassis, and the No-Ghost logo on its hood and front doors. Rivian has loaded the EV’s roof rack with a custom frame filled with screen-accurate sirens, spotlights, a radar dish and side tanks, as well as vintage emergency lights sourced and restored to complete the look. It’s so cool.

I couldn’t convince Rivian to sell me one of its custom Ecto-R1s — though that hasn’t stopped me from asking repeatedly — but the builds will be on display for fans to check out in person at Rivian retail spaces in Austin, Miami, San Francisco, New York, and Laguna Beach and Venice, California. The full list of events is on Rivian’s Halloween page.

title: Apple TV is adding two new features with iOS 27.2
snippet: iOS 27.2 is coming next week and brings two new features for Apple TV subscribers. Here’s what’s new. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.2 is coming next week and brings two new features for Apple TV subscribers. Here’s what’s new.

#1: Profiles come to iPhone and iPad, and with new characters

Apple TV is currently the only major streaming service that doesn’t offer user profiles on iPhone and iPad. But that’s about to change with iOS and iPadOS 27.2.

Profiles already exist in tvOS for big-screen viewing of Apple TV content, but now they’re coming to Apple’s other platforms too.

When you create user profiles on one platform, they automatically sync to others, letting you keep playback history, queues, and recommendations all personalized for each viewer. And if you set up a profile for your child, they’ll only see age-appropriate Apple TV content.

Alongside the expansion of profiles to more platforms, Apple has added a variety of new profile image options in iOS 27.2. Characters from Apple TV kids’ series like The Snoopy Show, Frog and Toad, and Stillwater are all now available. 

#2: Sign language support

Apple TV is taking accessibility a step beyond subtitle options by adding official support for sign language on select movies and shows.

With iOS 27.2, users can optionally enable American Sign Language (ASL) or British Sign Language (BSL).

You’ll find the option to enable sign language inside the Settings app under Apps ⇾ TV ⇾ Sign Language. It’s unknown how many Apple TV titles will support sign language initially, but it’s great to see the feature added.

title: Samsung’s new Fitbit competitor just leaked [Video]
snippet: Samsung has a new Galaxy Fit 4 fitness tracker in the works, and it looks just a bit more like an Apple Watch this time around. more…
fullText:
Samsung has a new Galaxy Fit 4 fitness tracker in the works, and it looks just a bit more like an Apple Watch this time around.

The Galaxy Fit lineup serves as a more affordable alternative to the Galaxy Watch series, offering a smaller, less advanced wearable that still serves core functions in fitness tracking and providing a clock face. The latest release was 2024’s Galaxy Fit 3 and it seems Samsung has a new refresh incoming.

Leaked images from The Cipher Project on Telegram give us a pretty good look at the Galaxy Fit 4 in three colors. The hardware itself isn’t all that different from Fit 3, but there’s certainly another half-step into Apple Watch territory this time, especially with the other two color variants and the adjustment to the curve in the watch band.

Android Authority also managed to uncover a video of the tracker, showing the band mechanism and sensors on the back. 

	

The Galaxy Fit 4 will have to face off against Google’s Fitbit Edge upon launch, whenever it might arrive, though its not-so-secret weapon could be pricing. Galaxy Fit 3 was just $60 when it made its debut in the US, and still sells for less than that even though Samsung has ended first-party sales.

title: Fitbit Edge doesn’t have Google Wallet because ‘less than 1%’ of Charge owners used it
snippet: Chicken, meet egg. Google has clarified why it didn’t include NFC and, in turn, Google Wallet support on the Fitbit Edge, and it just boils down to the fact that hardly anyone was using the feature. more…
fullText:
Chicken, meet egg. Google has clarified why it didn’t include NFC and, in turn, Google Wallet support on the Fitbit Edge, and it just boils down to the fact that hardly anyone was using the feature.

The ability to pay at the register with your wearable is nothing new, but NFC support on smartwatches and trackers has been pretty hit or miss in the past. Google supports the feature as a standard across the Pixel Watch lineup, and the last-gen Fitbit Charge 6 also supported the feature.

But, with the new Fitbit Edge, NFC support is gone and, in turn, so is Google Wallet.

It’s an interesting regression on Google’s part, so why the change? In a statement to Android Authority, Google explains that it really just comes down to a lack of people actually using this feature on the Fitbit Charge 6. 

	

Fitbit Edge does not offer NFC for payments. It was not widely used by our Charge 6 users — in fact, less than 1% reported using the feature on Charge 6 — so we prioritized other top features such as adding an altimeter and requested improvements.

Google says that skipping NFC left room to “prioritize” other features such as the Edge’s new altimeter, but it still seems like a shame to skip out on mobile payments for what is very much a “Pixel Watch Lite.”

	

Would you have used Google Wallet on the Fitbit Edge? Is it a dealbreaker? Let us know in the comments below.

Fitbit Edge launches on October 27, with pre-orders open now.

title: Google Photos rolls out customizable redesign of your ‘Collections’ tab
snippet: Following the floating navigation bar in July, Google Photos for Android is rolling out a big redesign that lets you customize the Collections tab. more…
fullText:
Following the floating navigation bar in July, Google Photos for Android is rolling out a big redesign that lets you customize the Collections tab.

The previous design started with a 2×2 grid. Favorites and Trash were at the top, while the other two shortcuts changed based on usage. Then there were large cards for Albums, On this device, People & pets, Wardrobe, Documents, Places, Stickers, and Moments. On Android, this was followed by a list: Screenshots, Videos, Recently Added, Archive, and Locked.

Old

This redesign of Collections is focused on customization. The first section is called “Pinned” and lets you choose which cards appear. By default, the carousel shows Favorites, Screenshots, and Trash. You also have the option to remove this section entirely. 

	

That’s followed by carousels for On this device, Albums, People & pets, Wardrobe, Places, and Documents. “View all” at the top-right corner lets you jump straight to the full grid or list view. Other options let you hide each section and rearrange the order in which they appear.

New

The “Other Collections” grid rounds out this page: Favorites, Screenshots, Moments, Videos, Recently Added, Stickers, Creations, Archive, Locked, and Trash. The “Reorder” button is found at the very bottom. 

This redesign is now widely rolling out with Google Photos 7.97. Instead of the usual Force stop, we’ve curiously been able to get this server-side update by restarting our devices and then opening the Photos app.

fullText:
Supply chain reports suggest that Apple has increased iPhone Duo orders by more than 40% in response to what the company described as “extraordinary” pre-order demand.

Delivery dates started slipping literally within a minute or so of pre-orders opening, and it wasn’t immediately clear whether this reflected high demand or poor supply. This latest report seems to point firmly to the former … 

Pre-orders opened on Friday and customers immediately reported receiving extended delivery dates, some of them into late January. Apple said that this was due to what it described as “extraordinary” demand for its first folding iPhone, but this is a phrase it frequently uses for new iPhone launches. The company also limited orders to a maximum of two per customer in a bid to tackle scalping.

As we expected, some of those ordering the new iPhone were subsequently given earlier estimated shipping dates. This may be explained by a DigiTimes report based on supply chain sources suggesting that Apple has ramped up production.

The report indicates that Apple expects strong demand to continue, and has boosted its shipment targets from 9.7 million to 14 million units over the first 12 months.

Early customers are going to have to contend with third-party apps not yet optimized for the device, but Apple says the situation is improving rapidly as developers get on board. The first reviews based on a week of usage present a consistent view, with app support one of five key takeouts.

The downgrade to Touch ID was another of these, but a report today says Apple is already testing iPhone Duo 2 prototypes with Face ID.

fullText:
It’s been a busy fall for Apple. iOS and macOS 27 arrived in September, iPhone Duo went on sale just a few days ago, and more Mac announcements are expected later this week. Between the new software and hardware, there’s plenty for Apple users to explore.

Of all these announcements, the iPhone Duo has arguably attracted the most attention. As the first iPhone with a fundamentally different form factor, it introduces new possibilities for how we use our phones. But new hardware is only part of the story. Just as important is how apps take advantage of it. For an app like Craft, which brings notes, tasks, and documents together in one place, the larger display and new multitasking capabilities open up interesting new ways to work.

Craft is ready for iPhone Duo from day one, with an interface designed to take advantage of its new form factor. And while the Duo is getting much of the attention right now, Craft has also seen a steady stream of improvements across iPhone, iPad, and Mac over the past few months.

And there’s an additional bonus for anyone looking to give Craft a try: 40% off for life with code 9to5Mac40, available through this exclusive 9to5Mac offer.

From quick notes to big ideas: Craft on iPhone Duo

Craft has always been developed specifically for Apple’s platforms, with the same features available across iPhone, iPad, and Mac, but an interface tailored to each device. That approach carries over to iPhone Duo, where Craft adapts between compact and unfolded poses.

In its compact form, Craft works much like it does on any other iPhone. You can quickly capture an idea, check off a task, or work on a document with the full set of editing and formatting tools. Unfold the device, though, and there’s suddenly much more room to work with. Writing, organizing information, and navigating longer documents all benefit from the additional space. The matte inner display with its nano-texture finish is particularly well suited to reading, especially when browsing through Craft’s richly styled documents.

The larger display is also a good fit for some of Craft’s more advanced features. Collections, for example, let you organize information in structured views, including Tables and Kanban boards. Being able to see more cards and information at once makes these views considerably more useful on the unfolded screen.

One of the Duo specific iOS features that has gotten the most praise from reviewers is the new side-by-side multitasking mode, and it’s particularly useful with Craft. You can keep a document open on one side of the screen and Photos on the other, dragging images directly into your document. Or open Safari alongside Craft to drag over text, images, and even entire web pages while researching a topic or putting together a mood board.

It’s a good example of how the new form factor can make familiar workflows feel quite different, without requiring an entirely new way of using the app.

Built for the entire Apple ecosystem

For those unfamiliar with Craft, it’s a productivity app that brings notes, tasks, and documents together in one place. You can capture ideas, organize projects, plan your day, and create polished documents to share with others, all within the same app.

Craft is available on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and even Apple Vision Pro, with fast syncing that makes it easy to move between devices. It’s also built to work offline, so you can keep writing or organizing your notes on the subway or during a flight. Your changes sync automatically once you’re connected again.

But Craft’s approach goes beyond making the same app available everywhere. Its interface and interactions are designed for each platform, whether you’re working with touch on an iPhone or using a keyboard and trackpad on a Mac. One of Craft’s strengths is how easy it makes it to create good-looking documents, without having to spend much time adjusting layouts or formatting. And if you want to share your work, you can turn any document into a website with a single click.

And of course, being so deeply integrated into the Apple ecosystem, Craft takes full advantage of Apple’s OS features. Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets keep frequently used content within reach, Shortcuts lets you automate common workflows, and Siri AI makes it possible to access and work with your Craft content without always having to open the app.

Craft keeps getting better, wherever you use it

While the iPhone Duo launch is a good reason to take another look at Craft, quite a bit has changed in the app itself over the past few months. Rather than focusing exclusively on adding new features, the Craft team has spent much of the summer revisiting existing ones, improving how they work and making everyday interactions faster and more consistent.

The team started by revisiting tasks. In Craft, tasks can live directly inside your notes and documents, keeping them close to the information they’re related to. At the same time, dedicated task views bring everything together, so you can see what’s due today, plan upcoming work, and keep track of tasks across different projects without having to open each document individually.

Templates have also become more flexible. You can start with one of Craft’s existing templates or create your own for recurring workflows, whether that’s meeting notes, project plans, or weekly reflections. You can now also assign a default template to your Daily Notes, so every new day starts with the structure you’ve chosen.

Another area where Craft has taken a somewhat different approach is AI. Rather than making it central to every interaction, Craft treats AI as an optional tool that users can incorporate into their workflow as much or as little as they like.

Craft Assistant is built into the app and can help with writing, editing, and working with information in your documents. You can use it through Craft’s built-in credit system or connect your own AI provider using Bring Your Own Key (BYOK). For those who prefer working with external AI tools, Craft also supports MCP, making it possible to connect your documents and tasks to other agents and build more customized workflows.

snippet: Apple has released HomePod 27.2, its latest software update for HomePod users. Here’s what’s new. more…
fullText:
Apple has released HomePod 27.2, its latest software update for HomePod users. Here’s what’s new.

HomePod 27.2 adds Sound Glow, Lock Controls, Mac speaker support, and more

It’s not often that HomePod gets a software update with new features. But that’s exactly what happened today with HomePod 27.2.

The latest software update, which you can install from the Home app on your iPhone, supports four noteworthy new features:

Sound Glow

Lock Controls

Mac speaker output

Apple TV surround sound (coming soon)

Sound Glow is a new feature that turns the top of your HomePod “into a visual canvas that glows and pulses in sync with the music, reacting in real time to bass and treble.” Apple adds, “The song’s album artwork from Now Playing generates a color-matched light experience that’s unique to every song, and users can pick a soundscape like rain to trigger bespoke animations for a soothing atmosphere.”

HomePod 27.2 brings Sound Glow to HomePod (2nd generation) and HomePod mini, and it will also be supported on HomePod mini 2 later this week. You can see a hands-on in our video below:

Lock Controls is a new setting that lets you disable touch controls on the top of your HomePod. If you have a small child in your household, or perhaps a cat, this new option lets you streamline all HomePod control through your devices and voice only.

Mac speaker output lets you set one or a stereo pair of HomePods as the default audio output for your Mac. Provided you have a Mac with Wi-Fi 6E or later, you can use this new feature and never need to manually connect via AirPlay again.

Coming soon: Four-speaker surround sound with Apple TV

Finally, coming soon is a new four-speaker surround sound feature with the Apple TV 4K (4th gen), which arrives November 13. HomePod 27.2 adds support for surround sound even though users will have to wait to try it.

HomePod (2nd generation) and HomePod mini 2 are both compatible with surround sound. You can even mix-and-match large and small HomePods in your setup as long as front and rear speaker pairs match. 

Apple explains: “four speakers work together with Apple TV 4K to intelligently recognize their position in the room so audio timing and levels are automatically calibrated to the space.”
